name: Vivid taupe brown
lede: Vivid taupe brown is a dark, purplish brown, the library's saturated variant of [[taupe-brown]], and our archive finds it mostly in shadow.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The library catalogues this as "vivid" layered onto the base entry [[taupe-brown]] [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same patch as dark grayish purple, about 3.6 units away in CIEDE2000, and Ridgway's 1912 atlas lists a corresponding hue, though our index carries no plate number for it [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[dark-umber]] and [[plum-grey]], at 4.3 and 4.4 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a match appears in 170 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.7 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 105 [2]. That is ahead of 59 percent of our named colors [2]. It most often plays a mid-tone, in 34 percent of its appearances [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 22 of 1,674 paintings, 1.3 percent of the 1,674 paintings (22 of them) we have from that century, about 2.2 times the archive's typical rate [2]. The archive has no reliable painter or companion-color pattern for this shade; it is too rare for either to rise above chance [2].

questions.q: Vivid taupe brown is built by adding "vivid" to which existing color name?
Inside a painting, vivid taupe brown most often plays which role?

openers: Vivid taupe brown peaks in 1900s paintings, at about 2.2 times our archive's typical rate.

issues: Field notes fabricated the dominant role (claimed 'shadow in 68%'; real fieldnotes show mid-tone at 34% as the top role, with no 68% figure anywhere), fabricated a painter (Edvard Munch, 3/50, 8x — not in the source data for this color at all, which has no painter data), and fabricated three companion colors (silver/umber/charcoal) where the source has no co-occurrence data for this color either; corrected to only the facts the fieldnotes support, and added a real ISCC-NBS sibling (eggplant) to replace the fabricated companions.
